# Glossary

<!-- Generated by tools/state.py glossary from glossary.jsonl. Do not edit by hand. -->

**aliasing** (chapter 1). Two or more descriptions that reach the same stored bytes, so a write through one is visible through the other.

**axis** (chapter 1). One independently indexed direction of an array.

**broadcasting** (chapter 1). Matching array shapes for an elementwise operation by reusing input elements instead of copying them.

**buffer** (chapter 1). A region of storage that an array interpretation reads and writes.

**byte address** (chapter 1). The position of a byte in the program's addressable storage.

**byte offset** (chapter 1). A distance in bytes from a stated starting point.

**checksum** (chapter 1). A summary computed from visited values, used to check that a traversal read the expected data.

**contiguous** (chapter 1). Laying out an array's logical elements in consecutive element-sized positions, with no gaps, in a stated traversal order.

**dtype** (chapter 1). The type and size of each stored element, such as a four-byte signed integer.

**element size** (chapter 1). The number of bytes occupied by one stored element.

**locality** (chapter 1). An access pattern in which nearby storage positions tend to be used close together in time.

**materialization** (chapter 1). Creating independently stored elements by reading a view in a stated traversal order.

**median absolute deviation** (chapter 1). The median of the absolute distances between individual samples and their median.

**metadata** (chapter 1). Descriptions of how to interpret stored bytes, as opposed to the values themselves.

**origin** (chapter 1). The byte offset reached when every index is zero.

**pointer** (chapter 1). A typed value that can refer to an object, a function or just past an array, or be null.

**rank** (chapter 1). The number of axes an array has.

**reshape** (chapter 1). A change of shape that preserves the element sequence in a stated traversal order.

**row-major order** (chapter 1). A traversal in which the last axis index changes fastest and earlier axes change more slowly.

**shape** (chapter 1). The ordered list of element counts along the axes of an array.

**slice** (chapter 1). A selection of positions along an axis using a starting index, a stopping point and a step.

**stride** (chapter 1). The signed change in byte offset caused by increasing one axis index by one.

**tensor** (chapter 1). An array with an ordered set of axes whose coordinates select stored elements.

**view** (chapter 1). An array interpretation that shares another object's storage instead of owning a copy.
